name: Beta 0.18.7.105
notes: Probe and Market Surge status move into their tabs; under the credits, their icons (▲ ◈, in tab order) stay grey and light up when a surge is ready or the probe is out

log.t: Probe and Market Surge status move into their tabs; under the credits, their icons (▲ ◈, in tab order) stay grey and light up when a surge is ready or the probe is out
Smelter: furnace cards keep one fixed layout, so picking an ore never moves the page, and every furnace shows one clear status line: Full speed, Slowed, Paused or Off
Every sideways list glides the item you pick to the middle, smoothly: planets, tabs, crews and furnace ores
Probe tab: tap 'Space probe' to zoom, like planet and station names; no more zoom buttons
Station tab: 'Parked at …' now sits under the station's name
The Research tab is now the Station tab: tap the station's name to zoom, and research sits in its own Research card
Planet tab: the zoom button is gone; tap the planet's name in the card to zoom, with the level line sliding under the name

Smelting is now a steady flow with bars/min and busy % per furnace, the Smelter gets a Balance window that picks the best ore for each furnace (research bars first if you like), and its dot only shows when something needs you
Tapping a planet's name in the panel flies to that planet's Close-up when you're not zoomed in
Furnaces no longer use ore that open research needs, so research ore counts hold steady instead of flickering; auto-sell keeps the furnace's buffer on top
The Smelter tab also shows its dot when a new ore is available to smelt
Every tab shows an orange dot when something on it has changed since you last looked, like the Events tab
Balance opens a window: a free rearrangement first, then a slider to buy upgrades on top, showing cost, income now and after, and payback time
The station and the probe zoom like planets: Close-up, Closer and Galaxy from a zoom button in their tab or a double-tap, centred, with the zoom locked and drag to turn
Double-tapping a planet or its name steps through the zoom levels like the zoom button, and the view glides smoothly when the panel opens or closes
Close-ups keep the planet in the middle of the screen with the panel closed, hold their zoom until you double-tap the planet or press Galaxy, and drag to turn the planet
New futuristic ore miners: angled hulls with glowing light strips, glowing wheels, a glass ore capsule and laser drills that fire while mining; crew badges are now graffiti tags on both sides
Crew stars under planet names are outlined in orange until every point that crew adds is placed, then solid
Zoom button: two close-up levels (Close-up, Closer), then Galaxy, on a narrower button
Zoom button: a sliding line replaces the dots, and the first two close-up levels stand further back
The planet zoom button has three close-up levels (Close-up, Closer, Closest), then Galaxy, and keeps one size
Red planet names now use the same whole-orbit check as the tuning chart and green names: red means ore would overflow somewhere in the orbit
Stars twinkle more slowly, at random moments
The background stars now show in front of the galaxy and twinkle, and the galaxy is a little brighter
Planet names turn green when they have hauling to spare: a Speed or Cargo point could move to Mine rate and the ships would still keep up
Removed the crew list from the Specialists card: it now shows how many crews are hired, and each crew's quirk sits under its name above the area it controls
Each crew's name now sits above the area it controls: points, perks and training programs
Fixed a crash when hiring an Instructors crew

Removed Handling, Dock training and the − 2 s docking perk and quirk: the 28 seconds of docking, landing and loading are always fixed, and upgrades only speed up the flight. Handling points come back as free points

Mining crews reworked: a planet's points now go into one pool that the Crew Chief (crew 1) allocates across every trait, each point costing a little more than the last. The Shift Crew (crew 2) adds 20 points and swappable perk slots; the Instructors (crew 3) add 20 points and run training programs: Dock training, Prospecting, Deep drilling, Logistics, Advanced shifts and Mentoring. Specialist roles and retraining are replaced: Dockhands and Prospectors become Dock training and Prospecting, and existing saves carry over

Fixed Balance leaving planets short of ships when they have big silos (Ore Silos or Deep Silos): it could push mining a few percent above what the ships carry, so the planet's name turned red. Balance and the chart now account for the silo filling up over time
Tuning chart: only the round handles drag the lines; touching anywhere else on the chart does nothing, so swiping over it scrolls the panel
Planet tab trait panes: the crew-name and Next lines are gone; the planet's total multiplier sits next to each trait's name, and the panes are shorter
Upgrade + and − buttons keep the same size in every state, including Maxed
Maxed upgrade buttons no longer show the 20 / 20 count
Planet tab: the selected planet stays in view in the planet list (after switching tabs, opening the panel, turning or resizing the screen, or a few seconds after you scroll the list yourself)
Tapping a crew, planet, furnace ore or tab that's partly off the edge of its list scrolls the list so it's fully in view; opening a user guide section near the bottom scrolls it into view

Balance keeps ships ahead: income is now worked out over a whole cycle with each planet's real silo, Balance only picks layouts where the ships keep up (then the most income), and when free moves can't get there it offers the cheapest points to buy (To keep up · Add) or says the crews need a hire, retrain or research. The red best-upgrade button and the drag handles use the same, more accurate model

Quieter updates: new versions come out once a day at 4 pm Central and install themselves the next time you open the game; only important updates ask, at most once a day, and the update message lists everything new since your version
Mining teams are now called mining crews throughout the game and the user guide
